🗓 **TAWG Daily Catch-up**
_2026-10-02 23:00 → 2026-10-03 23:00 UTC_

## ⚡ **Highlights**

> **DeepSeek-V2-Lite ran on Deucalion** — A large public model executed successfully on the group's own hardware, a concrete step toward verifiable inference at real scale. [tg:tawg:5189]

> **Cross-community convergence article published** — A post connecting independent efforts at SCITT/IETF, TAWG, and a Linux Foundation lab reached a public audience and extended the group's visibility across aligned communities. [tg:tawg:5198]

## 🤝 **What moved**

### zkIE / cuda-gkr
_A new CUDA implementation PR opened for review, building on a prior chain of foundational work._

- Jimmy Shi (@jimmyshi) opened PR #23 in zkIE (feature/cuda-gkr → main), introducing a three-level reciprocal square root approach that builds directly on Merlini's PRs #19, #20, and #21, advancing the group's zero-knowledge ML proving pipeline toward GPU acceleration. [tg:tawg:5165]

### Deucalion inference
_A confirmed model run on group hardware opened into forward capacity planning._

- Jimmy Shi (@jimmyshi) produced a rough capacity estimate for running DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on Deucalion using layer-based sharding, drawing on benchmark data from the DeepSeek-V2-Lite run at sequence length 512, giving the team a concrete basis for scoping the next large-model experiment. [tg:tawg:5176]

### cross-community outreach
_A public piece bridging TAWG with parallel accountability efforts moved from concept into circulation._

- Petchevere (@petchevere) drafted a piece on independent convergence across SCITT at IETF, TAWG, and a Linux Foundation lab, building a public-facing narrative that surfaces shared assumptions about trustless AI accountability to a wider audience. [tg:tawg:5146]

- Baby Blue Viper acknowledged Petchevere's published article, reflecting how the outreach work is landing and connecting the group's accountability framing to parallel external efforts in standards and open-source governance. [tg:tawg:5199]

### serializer-binding
_The scope of the serializer-binding implementation received a community-backed confirmation._

- Pavlo (@pavlentyy82) confirmed that the boundary encoded in the serializer-binding work matches the documented scope, giving the team shared confidence in that interface and removing a potential source of ambiguity for downstream integration. [tg:tawg:5157]

## 🚀 **Next up**

### 💡 **Ideas to follow**

- The cross-community convergence framing could grow into a recurring bridge between TAWG and standards bodies such as SCITT/IETF and Linux Foundation efforts
- Capacity estimates for larger models on Deucalion open a natural path to planning the next hardware experiment

### ✅ **TODOs**

- Review PR #23 for cuda-gkr in zkIE and progress it toward merge
- Follow up on any remaining open questions around the serializer-binding interface boundary

## 🤖 **Trusty's take**

> **Today's spark:** A new CUDA proving-pipeline PR landed directly on top of a completed chain of foundational work — a clean sequential handoff showing how building on each other's output keeps momentum flowing without a gap.
>
> When the commit history reads like a relay baton pass, the CI pipeline barely has time to catch its breath. ⚡
